War Dogs

By: Jana Marx | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We look at how a SA cricketer living in Ukraine escaped the war with his four dogs.

Unique Selling Point:
Real authentic footage of Kobus's journey with the dogs and we film him on location in Croatia. It's the human part of the Ukranian war people need to see.

Summary:
When Croatia inched towards a possible place in the FIFA World Cup final, and firecrackers banged around Zagreb as residents rejoiced, Kobus Olivier, SA club cricketer and former CEO of the Ukraine Cricket Federation, couldn’t help but remember lying on his bathroom floor with his four dogs … as Russian missiles rained down on the Ukranian capital, Kyiv. Until the bombs started falling, President Zelensky was still telling people to stay calm and war could be averted, but Kobus was monitoring western media outlets and saw the writing on the wall. While his Ukranian friends got cross when he warned them that war was coming, he was preparing - drawing all his money in cash from ATM's, stockpiling food and water for him and the dogs… he couldn’t fathom why the war caught people off-guard. We tell the incredible story of how Kobus fled Ukraine with his four dogs when it became clear that it was no longer safe as Russian forces advanced. It was captured in a moving documentary produced by Stefan Enslin, now on Showmax. Kobus was unwilling to leave his four fur kids behind – traveling for 4 weeks by car and crossing three borders to get himself and his dogs to safety. Under normal circumstances, this trip should take 17 hours. It’s now 9 months since Kobus's arrived in Croatia. He is facing new challenges, as he tries to start a new life. As the war moves toward its one-year anniversary, we meet Kobus at a critical moment of rebuilding his life. He doesn’t have any friends in Croatia. It’s a very lonely world. He left his whole apartment and all his earthly possessions in Kyiv. He doesn’t even know if the apartment block is still standing. He lost contact with everyone he knew back there. Signal problems? Have they died as result of the war? He has no way to find out. He’s still awaiting his work permit and currently living off money he earned as T20 World Cup Cricket commentator. The trauma of the war is something he cannot describe to anyone who hasn’t experienced it first hand – and it’s still giving him nightmares. What’s next for Kobus Olivier…and Ukraine? He says the bitter irony of the war is that as long as Ukraine keeps getting weapons and support (and now Ukrainian troops will receive training on the Patriot missile system in the US state of Oklahoma) …Putin will retaliate.

Press Release:


Surviving
Ukraine

South African former cricketer Kobus Olivier, moved to Kyiv in Ukraine and built himself a happy life, far from the turmoil of his home country.
He lived with his four dogs, worked a good job coaching cricket and loved how peaceful the country seemed to be. That is until the 24th of
February last year, when Russian President Vladimar Putin launched the first missiles into Ukraine – the start of a devastating war with no end in sight. In the weeks before, Kobus prepared for the worst while he waited for what he believed was the inevitable. Then as Russian forces continued to advance, Kobus began documenting his journey as he prepared to flee Ukraine for Croatia with his four dogs. His social media posts sparked an interest that had thousands of people around the world, rallying behind him and his four dogs. It’s the remarkable story of one man’s brave journey to survival.

Producer:
Jana Marx | Presenter: Claire Mawisa

Script:


… 3 beats

VO: A bitterly cold February morning…

VO: Eastern Europe is on edge as Russian forces advance into Ukraine.

KOBUS UPS: I've never heard anything like that in my life. And I knew immediately the war has started.

VO: In the capital Kyiv, South African Kobus Olivier takes his four small dogs for a pre-dawn walk.

KOBUS UPS: I took the dogs out at four o'clock that morning. We were outside for about two minutes when I heard these, I think it was about nine huge explosions.

VO: As Russian missiles strike, Kobus flees to his apartment …

Putin UPS: “I decided to conduct a special military operation…” https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_5YeX8eCLgA

ABC News UPS: 0;00 - 0.06: “Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, the largest invasion of a neighbouring country in Europe since WW2…” https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O-kHkhTe8Pw

VO: Kobus seeks out the safety of his building’s basement parking lot, but he’s told he can’t enter with all four dogs.

VO: So he bunkers down in his bathroom…

VO: Mattresses and pillows, a flimsy defence.

UPS DOGS IN THE BATHROOM: “We got enough food here for quite a while. Candles here, it’s actually looking very cozy. It’s gone quiet outside now, so the dogs are pretty calm, they are okay.”

VO: He begins recording his wartime existence on his cell phone.

KOBUS UPS: I thought if the worst happened, at least I've recorded our last minutes.

VO: Little knowing the extraordinary impact his social media posts will have.

LINK: It’s almost a year since Russia invaded Ukraine. But this story is not only about war and the terror it brings.
It’s about a man and his love for his four dogs and about friends being there when you need them most.

VO: Kobus was a South African career club cricketer who spent a decade living and working in 12 countries, before settling in Ukraine’s capital - five years ago.

Kobus UPS: "I just fell in love with Kyiv, I felt that unbelievable energy… It felt like my place, like I’m meant to be in this place…"

VO: He moved there with his elderly father, their rescue dog, Ticky, and all his worldly possessions.

VO: Kobus joined the Ukrainian Cricket Federation, and became a coach at a school where he also taught English

KOBUS UPS: "I had a good job in Kyiv, I was director of a private International School. I'm still the CEO of Ukrainian cricket, I was receiving a salary at the time."

VO: Before long Ticky had three puppies… Jessie, the quietest of them…

Kobus UPS: "Ollie is just a little bit of a crazy dog he is always climbing onto things. And then Kaya, the little black one is the smallest of the three. In Afrikaans we would say she she's really “hardegat”."

VO: Sadly, Kyiv would become his dad’s final resting place.

KOBUS UPS: "When my dad passed away and Kyiv it's sort of you know, it was his resting place. My little family were the dogs - my dog family started there. So Kyiv will always feel to me like it's my home."

BBC UPS: “Russian troops are closing in on the capital…”

VO: Even as the Russian noose tightens on Kyiv, Kobus is determined to stay.

VO: Besides, fleeing a war zone with four dogs seems near impossible.

VO: Playing classical music to drown out the sound of missile strikes, Kobus and his dogs hold out for 10 long days.

VO: But his friends are growing increasingly anxious.

LINK: In the professional cricket community you could live worlds apart, but you are never, ever alone. Cricket friends from all over the world supported Kobus.

CLAIRE UPS: “Well, I can tell you one thing for sure - he wasn’t smiling this hard when we were talking, so clearly it’s because you’re here in the room with us…”

VO: Former Proteas cricketer Daryll Cullinan is in touch daily on WhatsApp.

CLAIRE UPS: "Did you worry about his safety that he really was in danger?"

DARYLL UPS: I remember chatting to him sort of late one evening, he said, let me show you what happened tonight. 7;58 and you just saw these strikes in the distance - ‘twas like a movie! And I was thinking well, hang on. You need to think about getting out of here, pal!

VO: Kobus hunts for ways to join the mass of refugees fleeing to neighbouring Poland.

VO: He finds someone on Facebook willing to give him a lift…

CLIP UPS: “He will be outside your apartment as soon as…”

VO: …and he can take his dogs.

VO: Running a gauntlet of roadblocks and the threat of missiles and Russian gunfire ever-present - they eventually make it safe at last.

VIDEO UPS: “It feels like a million years ago that we were stuck up in the bathroom…”

VO: But, it’s not to be. Unbelievably, Poland decides to only accommodate Ukrainian refugees.

VO: Again, Kobus’s friends intervene, urging him to take the first flight out, but the airline refuses to take all of his dogs.

CLAIRE UPS: You couldn't even get the words out of your mouth when they said choose two dogs…

KOBUS UPS: When I heard about the two dogs I was absolutely in a state of shock. And…but immediately I started thinking okay, I've got to make a plan. I got this far…

VO: One final daunting option remains….


ACT 2 - The Road Trip & Help of Friends

VO: With the little money he has left, Kobus buys a car…and sets off to Croatia…via Slovakia and Hungary.

VO: Using location services, Daryll and his other friends follow his painstaking progress.

Daryll UPS: Some of the most anxious moments of my life was watching that dot …watching that dot move… watching that dot move…"

VO: A trip that Google Maps says should take no more than a day…stretches into a gruelling four week trek.

VO: But at his lowest moments, the kindness of strangers continues to surprise him - like the man who helps fix his car after hitting a curb…

VO: …and then moments of good fortune: A friend who happens to be South Africa’s ambassador to Ukraine helps him through the bureaucratic obstacles.

UPS clip: “Sjoe, Andre, okay, unbelievable, baie baie, baie, baie dankie, hoor…”

VO: Then, after what seems like forever, and amidst all the uncertainty and violence of war, Kobus and his dogs finally make it!

VIDEO CLIP UPS: “Just arrived at the border… Croatian border…”


ACT 3: Starting Over

VO: Kobus’ survival videos have become a documentary, War Dogs and I.

LINK: Cricket is all about endurance, mind over matter and resilience... invaluable tools that sustained Kobus on his 4 week long journey to safety.

DARYLL UPS: He's hit the ground running again, he’s found a way, he's found another way. And that doesn't surprise me, because he's a people's person, he’s out there. He finds a way to find people meet people and make, make things work.

CLAIRE UPS: I think, in a way, that was a bit of a silver lining for me that I took away - it was that your human connections can be your wealth.

KOBUS UPS: Absolutely, this war has really restored my faith in human beings - in my friends.

VO: Like the 18 million people displaced in the past year, Kobus is once again rebuilding his life.

VO: He’s landed a school teaching job in Zagreb… But the war still haunts his every day.

KOBUS UPS: It's been the most challenging of all my new starts. I don't speak the language. I knew nothing about Croatia.

VO: He’s left all he owes in his apartment in Kyiv.

KOBUS UPS: Some nights I can't sleep. It's still one of my big problems. I wake up throughout the night.

VO: But what he values most, he still has.

KOBUS UPS: I'm here, I’m alive. I'm healthy, I got out of the war, I'm safe. My dogs are with me. And this is really what is important in life.

VO: He finds someone on Facebook willing to give him a lift… CLIP UPS: “He will be outside your apartment as soon as…” VO: …and he can take his dogs. VO: Running a gauntlet of roadblocks and the threat of missiles and Russian gunfire ever-present - they eventually make it safe at last. VIDEO UPS: “It feels like a million years ago that we were stuck up in the bathroom…” VO: But, it’s not to be. Unbelievably, Poland decides to only accommodate Ukrainian refugees. VO: Again, Kobus’s friends intervene, urging him to take the first flight out, but the airline refuses to take all of his dogs. CLAIRE UPS: You couldn't even get the words out of your mouth when they said choose two dogs… KOBUS UPS: When I heard about the two dogs I was absolutely in a state of shock. And…but immediately I started thinking okay, I've got to make a plan. I got this far… VO: One final daunting option remains…. ACT 2 - The Road Trip & Help of Friends VO: With the little money he has left, Kobus buys a car…and sets off to Croatia…via Slovakia and Hungary. VO: Using location services, Daryll and his other friends follow his painstaking progress. Daryll UPS: Some of the most anxious moments of my life was watching that dot …watching that dot move… watching that dot move…" VO: A trip that Google Maps says should take no more than a day…stretches into a gruelling four week trek. VO: But at his lowest moments, the kindness of strangers continues to surprise him - like the man who helps fix his car after hitting a curb… VO: …and then moments of good fortune: A friend who happens to be South Africa’s ambassador to Ukraine helps him through the bureaucratic obstacles. UPS clip: “Sjoe, Andre, okay, unbelievable, baie baie, baie, baie dankie, hoor…” VO: Then, after what seems like forever, and amidst all the uncertainty and violence of war, Kobus and his dogs finally make it! VIDEO CLIP UPS: “Just arrived at the border… Croatian border…” ACT 3: Starting Over VO: Kobus’ survival videos have become a documentary, War Dogs and I. LINK: Cricket is all about endurance, mind over matter and resilience... invaluable tools that sustained Kobus on his 4 week long journey to safety. DARYLL UPS: He's hit the ground running again, he’s found a way, he's found another way. And that doesn't surprise me, because he's a people's person, he’s out there. He finds a way to find people meet people and make, make things work. CLAIRE UPS: I think, in a way, that was a bit of a silver lining for me that I took away - it was that your human connections can be your wealth. KOBUS UPS: Absolutely, this war has really restored my faith in human beings - in my friends. VO: Like the 18 million people displaced in the past year, Kobus is once again rebuilding his life. VO: He’s landed a school teaching job in Zagreb… But the war still haunts his every day. KOBUS UPS: It's been the most challenging of all my new starts. I don't speak the language. I knew nothing about Croatia. VO: He’s left all he owes in his apartment in Kyiv. KOBUS UPS: Some nights I can't sleep. It's still one of my big problems. I wake up throughout the night. VO: But what he values most, he still has. KOBUS UPS: I'm here, I’m alive. I'm healthy, I got out of the war, I'm safe. My dogs are with me. And this is really what is important in life.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We look at how a SA cricketer living in Ukraine escaped the war with his four dogs.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Real authentic footage of Kobus's journey with the dogs and we film him on location in Croatia. It's the human part of the Ukranian war people need to see.
metadata.Summary: When Croatia inched towards a possible place in the FIFA World Cup final, and firecrackers banged around Zagreb as residents rejoiced, Kobus Olivier, SA club cricketer and former CEO of the Ukraine Cricket Federation, couldn’t help but remember lying on his bathroom floor with his four dogs … as Russian missiles rained down on the Ukranian capital, Kyiv. Until the bombs started falling, President Zelensky was still telling people to stay calm and war could be averted, but Kobus was monitoring western media outlets and saw the writing on the wall. While his Ukranian friends got cross when he warned them that war was coming, he was preparing - drawing all his money in cash from ATM's, stockpiling food and water for him and the dogs… he couldn’t fathom why the war caught people off-guard. We tell the incredible story of how Kobus fled Ukraine with his four dogs when it became clear that it was no longer safe as Russian forces advanced. It was captured in a moving documentary produced by Stefan Enslin, now on Showmax. Kobus was unwilling to leave his four fur kids behind – traveling for 4 weeks by car and crossing three borders to get himself and his dogs to safety. Under normal circumstances, this trip should take 17 hours. It’s now 9 months since Kobus's arrived in Croatia. He is facing new challenges, as he tries to start a new life. As the war moves toward its one-year anniversary, we meet Kobus at a critical moment of rebuilding his life. He doesn’t have any friends in Croatia. It’s a very lonely world. He left his whole apartment and all his earthly possessions in Kyiv. He doesn’t even know if the apartment block is still standing. He lost contact with everyone he knew back there. Signal problems? Have they died as result of the war? He has no way to find out. He’s still awaiting his work permit and currently living off money he earned as T20 World Cup Cricket commentator. The trauma of the war is something he cannot describe to anyone who hasn’t experienced it first hand – and it’s still giving him nightmares. What’s next for Kobus Olivier…and Ukraine? He says the bitter irony of the war is that as long as Ukraine keeps getting weapons and support (and now Ukrainian troops will receive training on the Patriot missile system in the US state of Oklahoma) …Putin will retaliate.
